correctness.rationale: Under probability-sphere and latitude normalization, harmonic-polynomial branching gives four mutually orthogonal sectors, with exact moments and multiplicities. Strict monotonicities of the active pairs reduce each of three design intervals to one crossing. Exact rational witness inequalities and interval-enclosed roots decide dimensions 3..11; two globally positive shifted coefficient polynomials and rational upper-envelope separators decide every integer dimension \(d\ge12\). The standard-library exact checker passed 201 assertions; a separate Gaussian-Jacobi quadrature cross-check passed 140 comparisons. The infinite theorem rests on the analytic derivative and polynomial-positivity arguments, not on finite numerics.

value.rationale: A complete natural constrained sampling-design problem is solved for all dimensions: degree-three harmonics are the first odd pure band with two distinct interior nodal latitudes and four transverse sectors. The exact source of worst-case instability changes at three sharp dimension thresholds; uniqueness and a high-dimensional limit are established. This is more informative than checking one radius or optimizing a known three-sector quadratic formula, and it does not pretend to optimize full condition number or discrete finite sensors.
